sections.h2: Where is the Cambria County Recorder of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is on the first floor of the Cambria County Courthouse, 200 South Center Street, Ebensburg, PA 15931, and the phone is (814) 472-1473. Staff are in from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, though recording stops at 3:30 p.m. sharp. The office also answers information requests by phone.

Records date to 1804. Documents from 1986 to the present are searchable online through the county's Tyler portal, the index for 1924 to 1985 is on a separate historical site, and anything older than 1924 is available only in the office. There is no subscription fee to view, and print or download costs $0.50 per page.

After recording, the office scans each document and hands it straight back. It accepts cash or checks payable to Recorder of Deeds, and staff will quote recording fees or copy prices if you call ahead. Military discharge papers are recorded and copied for veterans free of charge.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Cambria County?
sections.html:
The county's current fee schedule is dated December 1, 2025 and is posted as a PDF on the recorder's page. The office quotes exact totals by phone, so call before you mail a package. Two surcharges are spelled out on the office's notices and apply to nearly every sale document.

Cambria County Recorder of Deeds charges named on the office's notices
ItemAmount or rule
Act 152 of 2016 fee on all deeds and mortgages$15.00, charged since March 1, 2017
Added charge since December 1, 2025$1.00 on deeds, mortgages, easements, satisfactions, assignments, leases, orders and similar documents
Print or download of an online record$0.50 per page
Recording cutoff3:30 p.m., Monday to Friday
PaymentCash or check payable to Recorder of Deeds

The $1.00 charge also reaches statements of adverse possession, condemnations, awards and bills of sale. The county's fee changes notice lists every affected document, so ask for it if your closing involves anything unusual.

sections.h2: Why does a Cambria County deed need UPI approval?
sections.html:
Since August 1, 2016, the county's Assessment Office has to approve a Uniform Parcel Identifier certification before many documents can be recorded. The list covers deeds, decrees of distribution, awards of real estate, mortgages, rights of way, easements, leases, condemnations, declarations of taking, consents, assignments of leases and rents, sewage and water permits, highway occupancy permits, statements of adverse possession and boundary line agreements. The Recorder will not accept those papers without the approval.

The Assessment Office is at 200 South Center Street and its phone is (814) 472-1451. A UPI staff member sits in the Recorder's office, and approval is unavailable from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m. each day. The office urges closers to email documents ahead of time for pre-approval, using the UPI address on its page.

  • Send the deed to UPI review before the closing date, not on the day.
  • Keep the parcel description identical to the prior deed.
  • Avoid a closing slot that depends on approval between 1:00 and 2:00 p.m.

sections.h2: How do you e-record or pay transfer tax in Cambria County?
sections.html:
The office takes e-recording for certain document types through Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, CSC Global and ePN. The recorder's page lists a phone number for each vendor. Paper originals can still be brought to the counter.

The Recorder also collects Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and distributes it. The state levies 1% of the value of the real estate, and local governments may add their own share, so ask the office for the combined rate that fits your municipality and school district. Some transfers are exempt, including certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy.

Both buyer and seller can be held liable for the tax, according to the state's Department of Revenue. Settle in the purchase agreement who pays it, and confirm that your closing agent has the funds in an accepted form.

sections.h2: What happens to Cambria County tax-delinquent houses?
sections.html:
The county Tax Claim office collects delinquent school, municipal and county real estate taxes and runs the tax sales. Its phone is (814) 472-1445, and it sits at 200 South Center Street. The Judicial Tax Sale for 2026 was scheduled for Monday, October 12, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. in Courtroom 1, with bidder registration ending October 2.

Since April 1, 2025, a $250.00 fee has been added to the costs of every property sold at an upset, judicial, private or repository sale, under Cambria County Ordinance 5 of 2024. Private sales are capped at 50 properties, and each bidder may list up to four per sale. For the 2025 tax year and later, delinquent school taxes in Cambria Township, Ebensburg Borough and Jackson Township, the Central Cambria School District, are collected by Portnoff Law Associates, at (866) 211-9466.

A seller who owes back taxes should get a certification from the Tax Claim office, and the office takes certification orders online. Ask the Tax Claim office what is owed for each tax year before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: Who handles assessments and homestead filings in Cambria County?
sections.html:
The Cambria County Assessment Office, in the courthouse at 200 South Center Street, keeps property records and values real estate for taxation. It does not set millage or collect taxes. The county is a fourth-class county under the General County Assessment Law, and the phone is (814) 472-1451 with hours of 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.

The same office runs the Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion program under Acts 50 and 1 and the Clean and Green preferential assessment program under Act 319. It posts an appeal form, appeal board rules, millage rates and a homestead application for 2026, along with the schedules for the 2026 appeal hearings. Sellers who plan to appeal before listing should read the board rules first.

  • Assessment Office: values property and takes appeals.
  • Tax Claim office: collects delinquent taxes and holds tax sales.
  • Recorder of Deeds: records the deed and collects transfer tax.

sections.h2: What is Cambria County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Cambria County is an older industrial county in the Appalachian Regional Commission area, and its home prices run far below the state's suburban counties. It covers 694 square miles, was created in 1804 and organized in 1807, and takes its name from the Latin word for Wales. Ebensburg is the seat, and Johnstown, the home of the old Cambria Iron Company, is the largest city.

Population peaked at 213,459 in 1940 and was 133,472 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 128,968. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 data show a median home value of $121,000, median household income of $58,418, median gross rent of $739 and an owner rate of 76.4%. Residents 65 and older make up 26.2% of the population, and 14.5% live in poverty.

Main roads are US 22, US 219 and US 422, plus PA 36, PA 56 and PA 53. Prince Gallitzin State Park and the trailhead of Laurel Ridge State Park are in the county. Winters are cold, with average January temperatures near 28 degrees in Johnstown and 24 in Ebensburg.

faqs.q: What time does the Cambria County Recorder of Deeds stop recording?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 3:30 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office stays open until 4:00 p.m. The office opens at 9:00 a.m. Monday through Friday. Plan the deed to arrive well before the cutoff.

faqs.q: Does Cambria County charge an extra fee on deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. A $15.00 fee applies to all deeds and mortgages under Act 152 of 2016, in place since March 1, 2017. Since December 1, 2025 an added $1.00 applies to deeds, mortgages, easements and many other documents.

faqs.q: Where can I search Cambria County deeds online?
faqs.a: Records from 1986 to now are on the county's Tyler web portal, linked from the recorder's page. The 1924 to 1985 index is on SearchIQS. Records before 1924 are available only in the office, and printing costs $0.50 per page.

faqs.q: Does a deed in Cambria County need approval before recording?
faqs.a: Yes. Since August 1, 2016 the Assessment Office has to approve the UPI for deeds, mortgages, easements, leases and similar documents. Approval is not offered from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m., so send the document in advance.

faqs.q: What extra fee does Cambria County add to tax sale costs?
faqs.a: A $250.00 fee is added to the costs of every property sold at an upset, judicial, private or repository sale since April 1, 2025. The charge comes from Cambria County Ordinance 5 of 2024. Call the Tax Claim office at (814) 472-1445 for details.
